subject: mathematics
question_text: Compute [i − j  j − k  k − i].

mark_split.label: Write the three vectors as rows
State the value and the reason

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.74, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 34. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives half the marks to the determinant and a full mark to naming the reason the answer had to be zero. Three evaluations agree at 0: the first-row expansion gives 1(1) + 1(−1) + 0 = 0; the third-column expansion gives 1(0 − 1) + 1(1) = 0; and computing (j − k) × (k − i) = i + j + k and dotting with (i − j) gives 1 − 1 + 0 = 0. The answer is the NUMBER 0, not the zero vector — a scalar triple product is a scalar. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would compute this — the determinant you write, and the one-line reason the answer had to be zero.

steps.label: Write the three vectors as rows
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write each vector as an ordered triple first; the missing component of each is 0.
steps.memory_tip: Each of the three has one zero component. Write the zero in its own column.
lines: The box product is the determinant

recall.must_convey: That the three vectors are written in components as the rows of a 3×3 determinant.
accept: write i minus j as one, minus one, zero and so on for the other two
the box product is the determinant with the three as rows
each vector has one zero component
moodu vectors ni components ga rasi rows ga pettali
set up the three by three determinant

steps.why: Written in components, the scalar triple product of three vectors is the determinant whose rows are their components.
common_mistakes: Writing i − j as (1, 1, 0) and losing the minus.
Reading k − i as (1, 0, −1) instead of (−1, 0, 1).

steps.label: Expand the determinant
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The middle term carries the cofactor's minus and the entry's minus, so it turns into a plus.
steps.memory_tip: A minus cofactor times a −1 entry gives a plus. Two minus signs meet in the middle term.
lines: Check: (j − k) × (k − i) = i + j + k,

recall.must_convey: That the determinant expands to 0, confirmed by the cross-product route.
accept: expand the determinant and get one minus one which is zero
j minus k crossed with k minus i is i plus j plus k
dotting that with i minus j gives zero
reject: write the three vectors as rows

steps.why: Computing the cross product first and dotting with the first vector must give the same number as the determinant, and it does.
common_mistakes: Getting the sign of the middle cofactor wrong and reporting 2.
Reporting the answer as the vector 0 instead of the number 0.

steps.label: State the value and the reason
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Naming the reason, that the three add to zero, is worth writing beside the answer.
steps.memory_tip: The three add to the zero vector, so they must be coplanar and the box product must be 0.
lines: so the three vectors are dependent

recall.must_convey: That the answer is 0, because the three vectors add to the zero vector and so are coplanar.
accept: the three vectors add up to the zero vector so they are coplanar
coplanar vectors have box product zero
the answer is the number zero
moodu kalipithe zero, so coplanar, box product zero
dependent vectors give a flat box of zero volume
reject: write the three vectors as rows

steps.why: A zero box product means the box built on the three vectors is flat, which is exactly what the three vectors summing to the zero vector forces.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer as a vector.
Saying the vectors are parallel; they are coplanar, not parallel.
